analysis: The PR is documentation-only (docs/threat-model.yaml). It adds a header comment (lines 43-45), asset A-018 (provider_serving_availability), boundary TB-012 (provider_to_local_addon_hold_socket, head lines 811-841) and, per the patch hunk at head 2305-2337, a T-059 threat that is outside the supplied excerpt. I examined the head text for units 8 and 9 (head lines 473-1395). TB-012 describes an owner-only 0600 AF_UNIX socket in a 0700 directory. It also describes per-request LOCAL_PEERTOKEN audit-token checks, same-UID enforcement and a Developer ID requirement for io.darkbloom.sandbox under team SLDQ2GJ6TL with the hardened runtime. A hold closes admission, reports draining status, unloads models, and does not send provider_drain or stop the App Attest worker. Leases run 30-600s, and active holds persist at 0600. The documented limitations are candid: same-UID code can tamper with the hold record and machine lock or extend a hold, add-on entitlements are not inspected, and leases use wall-clock time. The text also notes that DEBUG builds may add one configured identity, which is a build-time control, not a runtime one. This is documentation only, so no executable code or security control changes. The existing T-041 and TB-007 content is unchanged in this view, apart from the cache-storage text that was already there. I found no regression in the documented threat model. I could not verify three things: the actual add-on hold implementation under provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Addon/, the T-059 text, and coordinator handling of the busy fields (explicitly stated to be separate platform work). The next pass should check that T-059 and the A-018 mitigations match that code. The key points are the signature and requirement check, the DEBUG identity path, lease expiry versus machine-lock semantics, and the draining status the coordinator sees (T-053/T-057 interplay).
